subject: System Design
title: Cache-Aside Pattern
description: A fast breakdown of Cache-Aside Pattern for builders.

hook.text: The application checks the cache first. On a miss, it queries the database and stores the result in cache.

buildup.text: Cache-aside (lazy loading) puts the application in control of what goes into the cache and when.

discovery.text: Only requested data is cached. Unused data never wastes cache space. It's the most common caching strategy.

twist.text: Cache-aside can serve stale data. The database might change, but the cache won't know until the TTL expires.

climax.text: Cache-aside is simple, flexible, and works for most read-heavy applications out of the box.

punchline.text: Check cache, miss, fetch, store — the simplest pattern.

quiz.question: How does the cache-aside pattern work?
